scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: The idea in one sentence.
lines.say: The idea in one sentence.

lines.raw: A **C-CDA** is that discharge paper made digital and standard: one XML document with a fixed header and fixed, labelled sections, where each important fact is also stored as a **code** a computer can read.
lines.say: A C-CDA is that discharge paper made digital and standard: one X M L document with a fixed header and fixed, labelled sections, where each important fact is also stored as a code a computer can read.

lines.raw: CDA and C-CDA.
lines.say: C D A and C-CDA.

lines.raw: CDA (Clinical Document Architecture).
lines.say: C D A (Clinical Document Architecture).

lines.raw: An **HL7** standard (the same group behind HL7 v2) for clinical documents written in **XML**, a text format that wraps each value in named tags such as `<title>…</title>`.
lines.say: An HL7 standard (the same group behind HL7 v2) for clinical documents written in X M L, a text format that wraps each value in named tags such as <title>…</title>.

lines.raw: C-CDA (Consolidated CDA).
lines.say: C-CDA (Consolidated C D A).

lines.raw: The US set of CDA **templates**: agreed shapes for each document type and section.
lines.say: The U S set of C D A templates: agreed shapes for each document type and section.

lines.raw: Certified EHRs must be able to create and receive C-CDA documents (version **Release 2.1** is the one most widely used).
lines.say: Certified E H R's must be able to create and receive C-CDA documents (version Release 2.1 is the one most widely used).

lines.raw: Document vs message.
lines.say: Document versus message.

lines.raw: An HL7 v2 message reports **one event** ("Robert was discharged").
lines.say: An HL7 v2 message reports one event ("Robert was discharged").

lines.raw: A document is a **complete, signed snapshot** of care at a point in time ("here is everything about Robert's stay").
lines.say: A document is a complete, signed snapshot of care at a point in time ("here is everything about Robert's stay").

lines.raw: The common document types.
lines.say: The common document types.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **CCD** (Continuity of Care Document). When it is made: After a visit, at referral, or when a patient or another system asks for a summary. What it holds: A snapshot of the whole current record: problems, medicines, allergies, recent results, vital signs. Robert example: Bayou Family Medicine's summary after his February check-up.
lines.say: C C D (Continuity of Care Document). When it is made: After a visit, at referral, or when a patient or another system asks for a summary. What it holds: A snapshot of the whole current record: problems, medicines, allergies, recent results, vital signs. Robert example: Bayou Family Medicine's summary after his February check-up.

lines.raw: **Discharge summary**. When it is made: When a hospital stay ends. What it holds: Why the patient came, what was done, diagnoses, medicines on discharge, follow-up plan. Robert example: If Robert were admitted overnight, the hospital would send one to Dr. Nguyen.
lines.say: Discharge summary. When it is made: When a hospital stay ends. What it holds: Why the patient came, what was done, diagnoses, medicines on discharge, follow-up plan. Robert example: If Robert were admitted overnight, the hospital would send one to Doctor Nguyen.

lines.raw: **Referral note**. When it is made: When one doctor sends a patient to another. What it holds: Reason for referral, relevant history, current medicines and results. Robert example: Dr. Nguyen refers Robert to an eye doctor for a diabetic eye exam.
lines.say: Referral note. When it is made: When one doctor sends a patient to another. What it holds: Reason for referral, relevant history, current medicines and results. Robert example: Doctor Nguyen refers Robert to an eye doctor for a diabetic eye exam.

lines.raw: Others. When it is made: Various. What it holds: History and physical, progress note, consultation note, care plan and more. Robert example: Less common in plan data feeds.
lines.say: Others. When it is made: Various. What it holds: History and physical, progress note, consultation note, care plan and more. Robert example: Less common in plan data feeds.

lines.raw: Header and body.
lines.say: Header and body.

lines.raw: Every C-CDA has two parts.
lines.say: Every C-CDA has two parts.

lines.raw: The **header** says what the document is and who it is about.
lines.say: The header says what the document is and who it is about.

lines.raw: The **body** holds the clinical content, split into **sections**.
lines.say: The body holds the clinical content, split into sections.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Header**. What it holds: Document type and date; the patient (name, birth date, sex, the clinic's own patient ID); the author (doctor); the custodian (organisation that holds the original); the visit it describes. Analyst use: Match the document to a member; know its source and date.
lines.say: Header. What it holds: Document type and date; the patient (name, birth date, sex, the clinic's own patient I D); the author (doctor); the custodian (organisation that holds the original); the visit it describes. Analyst use: Match the document to a member; know its source and date.

lines.raw: **Body sections**. What it holds: Problems, Medications, Allergies, Results, Vital Signs, Immunizations, Encounters, Plan of Care and others. Analyst use: Find the clinical facts you need.
lines.say: Body sections. What it holds: Problems, Medications, Allergies, Results, Vital Signs, Immunizations, Encounters, Plan of Care and others. Analyst use: Find the clinical facts you need.

lines.raw: Inside each section there are two layers.
lines.say: Inside each section there are two layers.

lines.raw: The **narrative** is human-readable text, what a doctor sees on screen.
lines.say: The narrative is human-readable text, what a doctor sees on screen.

lines.raw: The **entries** are the same facts as coded, structured data that a computer can read.
lines.say: The entries are the same facts as coded, structured data that a computer can read.

lines.raw: A simplified piece of Robert's CCD (fictional; real files are longer and identify each code system with a long number called an OID).
lines.say: A simplified piece of Robert's C C D (fictional; real files are longer and identify each code system with a long number called an O I D).

lines.raw: The first lines are the **header**: what the document is (a CCD), its date, the patient and the author.
lines.say: The first lines are the header: what the document is (a C C D), its date, the patient and the author.

lines.raw: Each `<section>` has a code saying which section it is, a `<text>` **narrative**, and coded `<entry>` items.
lines.say: Each <section> has a code saying which section it is, a <text> narrative, and coded <entry> items.

lines.raw: The HbA1c entry carries the test code, the **value** and the **unit**.
lines.say: The H b A 1 c entry carries the test code, the value and the unit.

lines.raw: That is what a computer can use; the narrative is for people.
lines.say: That is what a computer can use; the narrative is for people.

lines.raw: Coded entries: the code sets inside.
lines.say: Coded entries: the code sets inside.

scenes.section: Coded entries: the code sets inside

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Problems. Code set usually used in entries: **SNOMED CT** (detailed clinical terms), often with ICD-10-CM alongside. Example for Robert: SNOMED CT `44054006` type 2 diabetes.
lines.say: Problems. Code set usually used in entries: SNOMED C T (detailed clinical terms), often with I C D 10-CM alongside. Example for Robert: SNOMED C T 4 4 0 5 4 0 0 6 type 2 diabetes.

lines.raw: Medications. Code set usually used in entries: **RxNorm** (clinical drug names). Example for Robert: An RxNorm code for metformin 500 mg oral tablet.
lines.say: Medications. Code set usually used in entries: RxNorm (clinical drug names). Example for Robert: An RxNorm code for metformin 500 mg oral tablet.

lines.raw: Results. Code set usually used in entries: **LOINC** for the test, plus value and unit. Example for Robert: LOINC `4548-4` HbA1c = 9.4 %.
lines.say: Results. Code set usually used in entries: L O I N C for the test, plus value and unit. Example for Robert: L O I N C 4 5 4 8 dash 4 H b A 1 c = 9.4 percent.

lines.raw: Vital signs. Code set usually used in entries: **LOINC** for each measurement. Example for Robert: Blood pressure 148/92.
lines.say: Vital signs. Code set usually used in entries: L O I N C for each measurement. Example for Robert: Blood pressure 148/92.

lines.raw: Allergies. Code set usually used in entries: RxNorm or SNOMED CT for the substance and reaction. Example for Robert: "No known allergies".
lines.say: Allergies. Code set usually used in entries: RxNorm or SNOMED C T for the substance and reaction. Example for Robert: "No known allergies".

scenes.section: Coded entries: the code sets inside

lines.raw: Narrative only is a data gap.
lines.say: Narrative only is a data gap.

lines.raw: Some EHRs fill the narrative but leave entries empty or vague.
lines.say: Some E H R's fill the narrative but leave entries empty or vague.

lines.raw: To a computer, a fact that is **only in the narrative** is almost as hidden as a scanned PDF.
lines.say: To a computer, a fact that is only in the narrative is almost as hidden as a scanned P D F.

lines.raw: Analysts measure how many documents from each source have coded entries before relying on that source.
lines.say: Analysts measure how many documents from each source have coded entries before relying on that source.

lines.raw: How health plans receive C-CDAs.
lines.say: How health plans receive C-CDAs.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Health information exchange (HIE)**. How it works: A regional network that passes clinical data between local providers (lesson 7). Plans that join can receive or look up members' CCDs and discharge summaries. Typical plan use: Care management after a hospital stay; finding missing results.
lines.say: Health information exchange (H I E). How it works: A regional network that passes clinical data between local providers (lesson 7). Plans that join can receive or look up members' C C D's and discharge summaries. Typical plan use: Care management after a hospital stay; finding missing results.

lines.raw: **EHR data feeds**. How it works: Under a data-sharing agreement, a provider group's EHR sends CCDs to the plan on a schedule, often nightly or weekly. Typical plan use: Quality measures, risk adjustment review, care gaps.
lines.say: E H R data feeds. How it works: Under a data-sharing agreement, a provider group's E H R sends C C D's to the plan on a schedule, often nightly or weekly. Typical plan use: Quality measures, risk adjustment review, care gaps.

lines.raw: **Medical record retrieval**. How it works: The plan, or a vendor, requests charts for specific members and dates. They may come as C-CDA or as PDFs. Typical plan use: Risk adjustment chart review, HEDIS record review.
lines.say: Medical record retrieval. How it works: The plan, or a vendor, requests charts for specific members and dates. They may come as C-CDA or as P D F's. Typical plan use: Risk adjustment chart review, HEDIS record review.

lines.raw: **HEDIS supplemental data**. How it works: Coded results pulled from C-CDAs (such as an HbA1c value) can count toward HEDIS quality measures when the source meets NCQA's audit rules. Typical plan use: Closing quality gaps that claims cannot show.
lines.say: HEDIS supplemental data. How it works: Coded results pulled from C-CDAs (such as an H b A 1 c value) can count toward HEDIS quality measures when the source meets NCQA's audit rules. Typical plan use: Closing quality gaps that claims cannot show.

lines.raw: HEDIS owns the measures.
lines.say: HEDIS owns the measures.

lines.raw: Which results count for which quality measure, and how supplemental data is audited, is taught in the HEDIS course.
lines.say: Which results count for which quality measure, and how supplemental data is audited, is taught in the HEDIS course.

lines.raw: C-CDA or FHIR?
lines.say: C-CDA or F H I R?

lines.raw: Lesson 4 introduced **FHIR**, the web API standard that sends small pieces of data called resources.
lines.say: Lesson 4 introduced F H I R, the web A P I standard that sends small pieces of data called resources.

lines.raw: Both are from HL7 and both carry clinical data, but they suit different jobs.
lines.say: Both are from HL7 and both carry clinical data, but they suit different jobs.

lines.raw: Lesson 6 covers FHIR in depth.
lines.say: Lesson 6 covers F H I R in depth.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Unit of data. C-CDA: A whole **document**. FHIR: Small **resources** (one patient, one result).
lines.say: Unit of data. C-CDA: A whole document. F H I R: Small resources (one patient, one result).

lines.raw: Format. C-CDA: XML. FHIR: Usually JSON (XML also allowed).
lines.say: Format. C-CDA: X M L. F H I R: Usually J S O N (X M L also allowed).

lines.raw: How it moves. C-CDA: Sent or fetched as a file through HIEs, EHR feeds and secure messaging. FHIR: Asked for on demand through web API calls.
lines.say: How it moves. C-CDA: Sent or fetched as a file through H I E's, E H R feeds and secure messaging. F H I R: Asked for on demand through web A P I calls.

lines.raw: Best for. C-CDA: A complete, signed snapshot at one point in time: a discharge, a referral, a chart for review. FHIR: Exactly the piece you need, now: an app, a single result, current coverage.
lines.say: Best for. C-CDA: A complete, signed snapshot at one point in time: a discharge, a referral, a chart for review. F H I R: Exactly the piece you need, now: an app, a single result, current coverage.

lines.raw: Where the rules require it. C-CDA: Certified EHRs must create and receive C-CDA. FHIR: CMS payer APIs (Patient Access, Provider Access, Payer-to-Payer) must use FHIR.
lines.say: Where the rules require it. C-CDA: Certified E H R's must create and receive C-CDA. F H I R: C M S payer A P I's (Patient Access, Provider Access, Payer-to-Payer) must use F H I R.

lines.raw: In practice, plans get both.
lines.say: In practice, plans get both.

lines.raw: Clinical data from provider EHRs and HIEs still very often arrives as C-CDA, because that is what certified EHRs have produced for years.
lines.say: Clinical data from provider E H R's and H I E's still very often arrives as C-CDA, because that is what certified E H R's have produced for years.

lines.raw: Data from the newer CMS payer APIs arrives as FHIR.
lines.say: Data from the newer C M S payer A P I's arrives as F H I R.

lines.raw: Many organisations convert C-CDA into FHIR resources so they can store everything one way.
lines.say: Many organisations convert C-CDA into F H I R resources so they can store everything one way.

lines.say: Worked example: Robert's C C D reaches his plan.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: **C-CDA** is the US template set for **CDA**, HL7's XML standard for whole clinical documents; certified EHRs create and receive it.
lines.say: C-CDA is the U S template set for C D A, H L 7 ' s X M L standard for whole clinical documents; certified E H R's create and receive it.

lines.raw: Common types: **CCD** (summary of the current record), **discharge summary** and **referral note**.
lines.say: Common types: C C D (summary of the current record), discharge summary and referral note.

lines.raw: A document has a **header** (what, who, when) and **body sections**; each section has a human **narrative** and coded **entries** (SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm).
lines.say: A document has a header (what, who, when) and body sections; each section has a human narrative and coded entries (SNOMED C T, L O I N C, RxNorm).

lines.raw: Plans receive C-CDAs through **HIEs**, **EHR feeds** and record retrieval, and use coded results as **HEDIS supplemental data**.
lines.say: Plans receive C-CDAs through H I E's, E H R feeds and record retrieval, and use coded results as HEDIS supplemental data.

lines.raw: C-CDA = a whole snapshot document; FHIR = small resources on demand.
lines.say: C-CDA = a whole snapshot document; F H I R = small resources on demand.

lines.raw: Plans usually receive both.
lines.say: Plans usually receive both.
